clue.text: Very old and cunning-one in a hundred

parts.note: arch means sly or knowingly cunning, as in an arch look

indicators.note: the word for one is placed inside the letters for a hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person as ancient and as sly as one in a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic belongs to a much earlier period, so it is very old.

clue.text: Man races with some anguish after a junior official

indicators.note: the races and the pain come after the single letter A

parts.note: the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
ache is a measure of pain, some anguish

explanation.surface: Someone races in anguish after a minor functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior member of an embassy's staff, a minor diplomatic official.

clue.text: Take inch off exceptionally thin stuff

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests the letters are set out in an unusual way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor is told to cut an inch off unusually thin cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiffon is a light, sheer fabric, so thin material or stuff.

clue.text: Anything at all out-moded

explanation.surface: Is there anything at all that is old-fashioned?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the word itself: it is an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word means anything whatever, and it is itself an old usage now seldom heard.

clue.text: What the gunman requires in transport over mountainous terrain

indicators.note: in a down light the transport sits over, above, the mountain feature

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport
a ridge is a long narrow mountain crest

explanation.surface: A gunman needs transport through hilly country.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun needs ammunition, and a cartridge holds the charge and bullet.

clue.text: Taking the motorway. Bet that's a blunder!

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, written here with the 1 read as I
a stake is money bet on an outcome

explanation.surface: A driver gambles that going by motorway was the wrong call.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is an error of judgement, which is what a blunder is.

clue.text: Doctor the tea or coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor is offered tea or coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine type of coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: One stands out for such building material

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A building material that stands out from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock used for building.

clue.text: The back-number is in time really torture!

indicators.note: the reversed number and the word is are placed inside a word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for number is read backwards

explanation.surface: Reading an old back issue of a magazine is real torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-number' looks like an old issue; 'back' reverses NO to ON, and ON plus IS goes inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer or cause intense pain, to torment or torture.

clue.text: See about the German left when getting on in years

indicators.note: the see's letters go around the letters for left and the German article

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see, in Cambridgeshire, England
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Look at how the old German man was left behind as he aged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone elderly is old, advanced or getting on in years.

clue.text: Pressed for a letting off

parts.note: the clue reads like someone begging to be excused a punishment, but it is the part of a gun squeezed to let off a shot

explanation.surface: Someone is urging the authorities to let them off.
explanation.definitionFit: On a firearm this lever is pressed to fire, or let off, the shot.

clue.text: Love-quarrels oft in pleasing — end." Milton (Samson Agonistes)

definitions.text: Love-quarrels oft in pleasing — end." Milton (Samson Agonistes)

parts.words: Love-quarrels oft in pleasing — end." Milton (Samson Agonistes)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's Samson Agonistes with one word blanked out; the missing word is the agreement or harmony lovers' quarrels end in

explanation.surface: A line of Milton about lovers' tiffs ending happily, with a word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the full line reads that love-quarrels oft in pleasing harmony end.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means harmony or agreement, the happy state a lovers' quarrel ends in.

clue.text: Where one may eat-eat if care is exercised

indicators.note: letters that are exercised are put through their paces and moved about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is told to be careful how they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is exercised' signals rearranging EAT IF CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is a place where people go to have a meal.

clue.text: Gather some men are rash irresponsible, and thoughtless

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are taken

explanation.surface: A remark that some men are rash, irresponsible and thoughtless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'raSH IRResponsible'. To shirr is a dressmaking term.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, to shirr fabric is to draw it up into parallel rows of gathers.

clue.text: His selection of winners is a matter of chance

definitions.text: His selection of winners is a matter of chance

parts.words: His selection of winners is a matter of chance
parts.note: reads like a hopeless tipster, but the 'he' is the random-number machine that picks British Premium Bond prizes

explanation.surface: A racing tipster whose picks are pure luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme whose prizes are drawn at random by a machine with a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment is the machine choosing Premium Bond prizewinners at random.

clue.text: A sober person will detain guys after stick-up that's the law

indicators.note: the teetotaller holding the men comes after the reversed stick
in a down light up means the word for stick is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cane is a stick

indicators.note: the teetotal letters detain, hold inside them, the word for guys

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal, a person who doesn't drink
men are guys

explanation.surface: A teetotaller holds some men up during a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' looks like a robbery; 'up' reverses CANE to ENAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is a law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Find the recording too yukky initially

parts.note: a disc is a record, a recording
over can mean too, as in over-cautious

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone finds a record they think is rather too yucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, so the noun find is a synonym.

clue.text: Content about the pupil's environment, so held to scorn

indicators.note: the word for content goes around the eye part

parts.note: sated means satisfied, content
the iris is the coloured ring surrounding the pupil of the eye

explanation.surface: A satisfied teacher thinks about a pupil's surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild, but it is the pupil of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to ridicule them, to hold them up to scorn.

clue.text: Will's disturbing statement

indicators.note: disturbing the letters means throwing them out of order

explanation.surface: Someone named Will has made an upsetting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will's' reads as a man's name with a possessive; it is the word will, followed by 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One's last will and testament is the legal document disposing of one's estate.

clue.text: Everybody entering the exam wanted to be highest

indicators.note: entering means one word goes into another

parts.note: a test is an exam
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone sitting the exam wanted to come top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallest means of the greatest height, so highest.

clue.text: The cat seems AI-fancy!

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate, so the letters are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A cat seems to be a fancy breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text read 'Al', but the anagram needs the capital I of AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of cat with blue eyes and a pale coat.

clue.text: Register always filled in by conservationists

indicators.note: the word for always has the conservation letters placed in its middle

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
the NT, National Trust, is the British body that conserves historic buildings and land

explanation.surface: A register that conservation volunteers always fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: To register a name or result is to enter it in a list or record.

clue.text: Working also with swimmers

parts.note: too means also
ling are sea fish, swimmers

explanation.surface: Working alongside the swimmers too.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooling is decorative working of leather or metal with tools.

clue.text: Turner can appear retrogressive just the same

indicators.note: says the word reads the same when its letters are run backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Turner's work appears to look backward but stays the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter but is a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates, so a turner.

clue.text: Fifty-a quarter, no less?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
east is one of the four quarters, or cardinal points, of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone haggling asks whether fifty minus a quarter is the minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash looks like a minus sign; it only joins the pieces. The definition comes from 'at least', meaning no less.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at least' means not less than a stated amount, so the word stands for no less.

clue.text: Have sport with a flighty creature, then a set-to

parts.note: a lark is a bird, a creature of flight
a bout is a fight or set-to

explanation.surface: Someone plays with a skittish animal before a scuffle breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to play around boisterously, to have fun or sport.

clue.text: Enabled a man to find oblivion

parts.note: let means allowed, enabled
he is a man

explanation.surface: A man is allowed to forget.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the river Lethe in Hades made those who drank from it forget their past.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking from this underworld river brought forgetfulness, so it stands for oblivion.

clue.text: Move in a dream, bleary-eyed

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone walks dreamily, still half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to move along slowly and at an easy pace.

clue.text: Great mountain girl accompanying others

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A big-boned girl joins the rest of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest peak on Earth, in the Himalayas, is the greatest of mountains.

clue.text: Overturned bus is in the way, but keep going

indicators.note: a vehicle that is overturned is upside down, so in a down light this word is turned back to front
the word is sits inside the abbreviation for a way, as the clue says it is in the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A bus on its side blocks the road but drivers press on.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to keep going, to manage to survive on limited means.

clue.text: The boards will get the rate adjusted

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted, changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Floorboards come with a revised price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' is a standard expression for the stage, and so for the acting profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards means acting on stage, so the boards stand for the stage or drama.

clue.text: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom

definitions.text: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom

parts.words: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom
parts.note: reads like a business on its last legs scraping the barrel, but describes a vessel that clears mud from a riverbed

explanation.surface: A firm whose managers keep scraping the bottom of the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: This boat scoops silt from the bed of a harbour or river, literally scraping the bottom.
